Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

pass verb

hand something to someone

also hand me, pass me, pass the salt, hand me that food, hand over, hold out, hand me the book, pass around, pass round, pass the bread

classical

Hor. Ep. 1.18.92: pōcula (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Deiot. 8: dexteram alicui (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 99: porrige mihi illum cibum

porrigō, porrigere, porrēxī, porrēctum

verb, third conjugation, transitive: alicui aliquid

hold out, hand, pass

Lewis & Short: “to hold forth, reach out, to offer, present”. At table the short way is cedo (give it here).

Other words

  • circumferō, circumferre, circumtulī, circumlātum — pass round (a dish, a cup)

    verb · also used · classical · Plaut. Pers. 5.2.45: age circumfer mulsum, pass around the mead (Lewis & Short); Traupman 357

Examples

  • Porrige mihi illum cibum.

    Hand me that food.Traupman 99

  • Librum cedo (cette).

    Hand me the book.Traupman 33

  • Porrige pānem, quaesō.

    Pass the bread, please.Traupman 357

  • manum porrigere

    to reach out the handTraupman 369

See also give it here!.
